Used to drink everyday, quit three years ago. There was no rock bottom. I got drunk and stoned everyday for 20 years. Always had good jobs( well shitty factory jobs, but really y good pay). I just started realized I spent twenty years going nowhere, hanging out with the same going nowhere people, telling the same stories over and over again. It had been a long long time since we went anywhere or did anything new or adventurous. Just go to the job we hate, get high at lunch, get off work, smoke joint, go to bar, get drunk, rinse, repeat. Weekends were sleep all day, wake up, get high, watch sports, eat garbage, get fat, go to bar get drunk, pass out , shit now it's sunday, lay around all day and get high or go to the bar and have a few while watching the early games. Get high, go to bed sad and angry that I had to get up for work on Monday morning.

So I was a functioning alcoholic\stoner,in the sense I went to work and payed my bills. But I had no savings, all of my relationships were basically two people who were either drunk or high together and liked to fuck, and all my friends were just other people who settled into the rut of work, drink, smoke, work, drink,work,drink. We were this little team of losers who thought we were cooler then everybody else, when in reality we had so little going on in our lives that we must have seemed boring to outsiders. When new new people came around it was just an excuse to tell those same old "remember that time..." stories we had been telling for decades. Hell, I started noticing my friends would insert themselves into stories when they weren't even there for the actual event. To be honest, I've heard some stories so many times, I don't even now if I was there or not.

I never did rehab or declared I was gonna be sober, I just stopped hanging out with those people as much (eventually, not at all), and didn't buy any weed or go to the bar. Quit the job I hated, made new friends, then all of a sudden I notice it's Christmas, and I hadn't drank or smoked since 4th of July. About six months sober. Then it's 4th of July. Damn it's been a year. Well it will be four years in July I guess, but it's not like it's a thing, just once in a while I realize how long it has been. I have had about 5 beers in the last three and a half years and went to a bar once, it just doesn't seem fun anymore.

I drank about 4 bottles of Jack Daniels and smoked half ounce of weed and a dozen packs of cigarettes a week for twenty years, now I don't drink or smoke. Once I got over the idea I was missing something by not going to the bar, I didn't miss any of it at all. But I realized that out of 365 nights at the bar, about 358 of them are the same boring thing. Maybe in a good year, about five days a year something bgood happens, blowjob from a hot girl in the parking lot, win a bet on a football game, get in a fight and win... if vyou look back honestly, it's 99% sitting at the bar with the same people, doing the same thing day after day.

I don't miss booze at all, don't even think about it. Occasionally, I miss getting high, but figure with my luck, after one night of fun, I would have a drug test come up, so why risk it. I don't even know who I could get it from these days. But if they legalize it in my state, maybe I would partake once in a while.

I personally think I drink to much, but I'm conflicted by the idea it helps more than it hinders. Some of my most productive days or even months have been fueled by booze. I've never been black out drunk but the right buzz can really help me get through the day.
